Heat Training Practices in Elite and World-Class Athletes: A Review of Preparation Strategies for Competition in Hot Outdoor Environments
abstract: Abstract Heat acclimation (artificial exposure) and acclimatization (natural exposure) are key strategies for elite and world-class athletes preparing to compete in hot outdoor environments, aiming to reduce performance impairments and risk of heat illness. Evidence-based guidelines, primarily derived from laboratory studies in non-elite cohorts, recommend 10–14 consecutive days of heat exposure (60–90 min per day), initiated at least 2 weeks before competition in the heat, or earlier if re-acclimation is possible closer to the event. Sessions should elicit sustained elevations in core and skin temperature, skin blood flow, and sweating. However, logistical constraints, training demands, and tapering often limit protocol implementation in elite and world-class athletes, prompting the adoption of alternative approaches. This review synthesises observational studies documenting heat training practices in these athletes and evaluates their alignment with current guidelines. Eleven of the 12 studies included sport-specific heat exposure within preparation for competition in hot environments, often in similar or more severe environmental conditions than competition, with five studies incorporating post-exercise passive heating. However, heat intervention design, session structure, and monitoring of thermal and cardiovascular strain varied widely, with many reports lacking sufficient detail to determine their effectiveness at inducing and retaining adaptations outside laboratory-controlled settings. Nonetheless, initial reports indicate that classical markers of heat adaptation such as reduced exercise heart rate and core temperature, and increased plasma volume, are commonly observed. title: A mixed-methods comparison of physical education curriculum reforms and structure: teachers’ voices from China and Pakistan
abstract: Purpose Guided by Comparative Curriculum Theory, the current study examined and compared PE teachers’ perceptions of curriculum reforms and structure at the secondary school level in China and Pakistan. Methods An explanatory sequential mixed -methods research design was used in this study. The study combined a cross-sectional survey of 434 PE teachers (217 from China and 217 from Pakistan) with qualitative in-depth interviews involving 14 PE teachers (7 from China and 7 from Pakistan). Quantitative data were analyzed statistically, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically to provide a deeper understanding of the survey findings. Results Both datasets revealed significant differences across all dimensions between China and Pakistan. Teachers from China reported more positive perceptions regarding the PE curriculum reforms and structure of PE. In contrast, Pakistani teachers reported less favorable perceptions of PE curriculum reforms and structure at the secondary school level. The qualitative findings revealed differences in curriculum governance, organizational coordination, and implementations capacity between the two countries. Implications Findings suggest that effective PE curriculum reforms not only depends on curriculum design bur also on governance arrangement and institutional support. Systematically aligned curriculum systems may appear to enhance coherence and effective implementation in PE, while inconsistent and outdated structure may limit the effectiveness of reform. These highlight the need and importance of context-sensitive policy development and stronger implementation support to improve secondary school PE.

title: Sex differences in psychological readiness returning to sport after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Psychological readiness is an important component of return-to-sport (RTS) assessment following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR). Although sex differences in psychological readiness have been reported, the available evidence remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare psychological readiness between male and female patients following ACLR and examine potential variation according to postoperative follow-up duration, population type, and surgical procedure. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Observational studies of patients undergoing ACLR were eligible if psychological readiness was assessed using the ACL-RSI or its validated short version and sex-specific data were available for quantitative comparison. Random-effects meta-analysis using Hedges’ g was performed. Prespecified subgroup analyses, leave-one-out sensitivity analyses, methodological quality assessment, and publication bias assessment were conducted. Results Twenty studies involving 4,000 participants (2,381 males and 1,619 females) were included. Male patients demonstrated significantly greater psychological readiness than female patients, with a small effect (Hedges’ g = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.09–0.38; p = 0.003; I 2 = 64.0%). No significant subgroup differences were observed according to postoperative follow-up duration ( p = 0.443), population type ( p = 0.212), or surgical procedure ( p = 0.764). Conclusion Male patients demonstrated slightly greater psychological readiness to return to sport following ACLR than female patients. title: Building resilience through blue exercise
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: This article examines how municipalities can facilitate blue exercise while balancing public health objectives, safety considerations, and individual responsibility in urban waterfront environments. Increasing urbanization and a growing interest in nature-based recreation have led cities, including Oslo, to transform former industrial waterfronts into accessible spaces for bathing, swimming, and social interaction. Research consistently highlights the health benefits of blue spaces, including enhanced physical activity, stress reduction, and improved mental well-being. However, these environments also introduce inherent risks related to water environments, raising questions about safety and accountability. Using a discourse-analytical framework informed by social constructivism and Foucauldian perspectives on power and knowledge, this study analyzes how risk, safety, and responsibility are constructed across municipal policies and legal. Empirically, the study draws on two Norwegian court cases involving accidents at urban waterfronts, as well as the “Safe Waterfront” guideline developed by Oslo municipality. These sources reveal differing interpretations of municipal liability and user responsibility. In one case, the municipality was held liable due to inadequate warning of a hidden hazard in a heavily used bathing area. In another, the Supreme Court emphasized personal responsibility, ruling that sufficient warnings had been provided and that users must assess risks themselves. The findings highlight a central tension between promoting accessible, attractive waterfronts and ensuring adequate safety. title: Comparison of automated and manual performance analysis tools in amateur padel: a descriptive case study
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Background Automated match-analysis systems increasingly provide technical-tactical reports in padel, but their agreement with manual observation remains unclear. The aim was to describe discrepancies between aggregate match statistics displayed by Padmi and manual observational coding in amateur padel. Methods Three amateur male matches involving one focal player were retrospectively analysed from video using the Padmi app (version 1.3). Six shot types (forehand, backhand, forehand volley, backhand volley, bandeja, smash) and three outcome categories were coded manually and compared with Padmi's aggregate reports. Signed and absolute differences were calculated for shot frequencies and percentage-point differences for outcomes. Shot-level agreement metrics were not calculated because raw Padmi event-level data were unavailable. Results Manual coding identified 891 shots, whereas Padmi displayed 757 (−15.0%). Padmi displayed fewer shots in all matches (−11.4% to −19.2%). Discrepancies varied by shot type: forehand −28.3%, backhand −20.0%, bandeja −3.5%, smash −44.8%, forehand volley +27.2%, backhand volley +5.9%. Overall outcome distributions were similar, but larger shot-specific discrepancies emerged for the smash, bandeja, and forehand volley. Conclusions Padmi's user-facing aggregate statistics differed from manual coding in this small case study. Automated reports may be useful for broad feedback but require cautious interpretation and further independent validation for detailed technical-tactical decisions.

title: Editorial: The relationship between human energy supply and environmental and training factors
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Human energy supply and its interactions with external environments and training strategies represent a cross-cutting topic spanning sports science, environmental physiology and military operational medicine. This paper summarizes a Frontiers Research Topic focused on human energy supply under complex conditions. The Research Topic addresses five research directions: training-induced energy metabolism mechanisms, training equipment for energy optimization, environmental effects on energy expenditure, assessment of energy limits in special environments, and translational research in sport and military scenarios. The included articles adopt diverse methods including metabolomics, ergometer testing and qualitative investigation, covering extreme settings such as cold, high altitude and desert. Contributions originate from research institutions across China, Ireland, Greece and Sweden. This Research Topic advances interdisciplinary communication and provides theoretical support for optimizing athletic performance and military operational efficiency, while identifying existing bottlenecks including ethical constraints and challenges in real-world data acquisition.

title: Molecular diversity and structural profiling of the EmrD efflux pump in multidrug-resistant uropathogenic Escherichia coli
abstract: Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) presents a significant therapeutic challenge due to increasing multidrug resistance (MDR). While acquired resistance mechanisms are well-documented, the genetic variability of intrinsic efflux pumps like EmrD remains less characterized. This study investigated the genomic diversity and structural conservation of the EmrD transporter in ten clinical MDR isolates from the Kurdistan Region, Iraq. Isolates were screened for the emrD and β-lactamase genes, followed by emrD sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and in silico protein modeling. Results confirmed the universal presence of emrD alongside multiple resistance genes. Phylogenetic analysis identified notable local genetic diversity, including a highly divergent lineage (DUH 11). Protein modeling mapped non-synonymous substitutions to transmembrane helices 6 and 12, regions critical for the “rocker-switch” conformational changes required for substrate translocation. These findings suggest that while EmrD is a stable component of the MDR machinery, localized genomic divergence may potentially influence efflux efficiency among clinical lineages, warranting future functional validation.

title: Co-designing a post-discharge intervention to improve mobility recovery among patients with lower limb fractures using human-centered design in greater Kampala, Uganda
abstract: Introduction Lower limb fractures are a major cause of functional limitation and require coordinated post-discharge care to support recovery and prevent complications. In low- and middle-income countries, including Uganda, continuity of care after discharge is often limited by health system constraints, socioeconomic barriers, and community barriers. This study aimed to co-design a post-discharge intervention to improve recovery among patients with lower limb fractures in Greater Kampala, Uganda, using a Human-Centered Design (HCD) approach. Methods A qualitative exploratory study guided by the HCD participatory and iterative framework was conducted between July and December 2025. Stakeholders including healthcare providers, community health workers, patients, and caregivers participated in focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and in-depth interviews to explore their experiences, needs, and challenges related to post-discharge care. Stakeholders subsequently participated in an iterative co-design process to prioritize and refine intervention components. Data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically using NVivo version 15. Results Several interconnected barriers to post-discharge care were identified, including discontinuity of care after hospital discharge, inadequate discharge information, transportation challenges, community and family influences on treatment decisions, use of traditional bone setters, and health-system limitations. title: Age-related slowing of sensorimotor reaction time in masters track and field athletes
abstract: Introduction Masters athletes offer a powerful model for understanding how lifelong training shapes age‑related changes in reaction time (RT), a key indicator of sensorimotor performance. Purpose This cross-sectional study examined RT in masters track and field athletes across age, sex, RT tasks of varying complexity, and event disciplines (endurance, power, sprint) Methods A total of 182 competitors (82 females) from the 2025 World Masters Athletics Championships completed four RT tasks using a wireless light-based testing system. Results RT increased progressively with age across all tasks, with the slowest responses consistently observed in athletes ≥80 years old. Female athletes demonstrated slower RT than males, and RT increased systematically with task complexity. Sprint athletes showed faster RT than endurance athletes overall, although event‑specific differences did not persist within age groups. Age was positively associated with RT in all tasks (r = 0.41–0.53), with similar correlation strengths between sexes. Quadratic age effects emerged selectively in male athletes for two-hand simple and step-choice tasks, suggesting accelerated slowing at older ages in tasks requiring greater motor coordination. Linear regression models indicated that RT increased by approximately 3.3–3.6 ms per year of age after adjusting for sex, task, and event discipline, while body composition variables were not significant predictors. Conclusions Although lifelong training is associated with better sensorimotor performance, slower RT remains evident in masters athletes, with consistent sex differences and minimal influence of event discipline.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and county-level coordination between sports-related intangible cultural heritage and tourism development in the Wuling Mountain Area, China
abstract: Sports-related intangible cultural heritage (SRICH) can support culturally grounded tourism, but its county-level alignment with tourism development remains unclear in ethnically diverse mountain regions. This study examined 71 county-level units in China’s Wuling Mountain Area in 2010, 2015, 2019, and 2024. Geographical concentration, kernel density estimation, and standard deviational ellipses traced the administrative distribution of officially recognized SRICH records. Entropy weighting, coupling coordination, relative-balance diagnosis, and Moran’s I assessed their county-level relationship with tourism development. SRICH coverage expanded and geographical concentration declined, while county-represented density peaks increased within a broadly stable regional configuration. Tourism development rose rapidly before 2019 and more slowly thereafter, retaining a marked core–periphery structure. Mean D increased from 0.192 to 0.403; 62.2% of this change was associated with counties entering the official inventory after 2010. Within the baseline-covered cohort, the joint levels of the two subsystems increased, whereas relative balance changed little, and SRICH-lagging counties remained predominant. All three indices showed significant positive global spatial autocorrelation, while FDR-adjusted local clusters were sparse and none remained significant in 2024. The results inform differentiated cross-provincial safeguarding and tourism planning, with greater attention to counties where the two subsystems follow different trajectories. The coupling coordination degree D is interpreted as a comparative measure of the recorded joint levels of SRICH and tourism development.

title: Decision-Making in Basketball: The Interplay between Cognitive Processes and Motor Execution
abstract: This study aimed to explore the relationship between dribbling behavior preceding passing and shooting patterns, and its implications for the interplay between decision-making efficiency and motor execution across four competitive basketball levels: the National Basketball Association (NBA), the EuroLeague, and European national teams, and the under-16 (U16) and under-18 (U18) European national teams. A total of 32 games (eight from each level) were analyzed to identify performance variables associated with success. Actions involving zero dribbles and sequences of three or more dribbles (3+) emerged as the most effective offensive patterns, reflecting the complementarity between rapid, intuitive decisions and deliberate, well-planned actions. Moreover, at the higher competitive levels, assists were more frequently produced following zero-dribble situations, underscoring the efficiency of quick, collective ball movement among elite players. Professional players were more likely to draw fouls during extended dribbling sequences, suggesting greater technical adaptability compared to lower competitive level players. Overall, these findings emphasize the integration of decision-making and motor execution as hallmarks of basketball expertise, highlighting the importance of developing both intuitive and deliberate decision processes in training.

title: Visual Search Strategies and Decision-Making in Highly Trained Female Youth Basketball Players: A Quasi-Experimental in Situ Study of Gaze Behavior during Pick-and-Roll Plays
abstract: This study explored how U16 female basketball players direct their visual attention and make decisions during side pick-and-roll situations under realistic game conditions. Twelve experienced players participated in 4v4 scenarios, where defensive strategies were systematically varied to reflect authentic tactical challenges. Using Pupil Core eye-tracking glasses operating at 120 Hz, we recorded gaze behavior without restricting natural movement on the court. Gaze data were synchronized with nine predefined tactical areas of interest using the surface tracker plugin, enabling detailed analysis of visual search behavior in dynamic environments. Time-series, entropy, and gaze transition analyses revealed that offensive decisions were closely shaped by defensive constraints. “Pass to Roller” and “Pass to Corner” were the most frequent responses, depending on the defensive strategy in place. Players’ gaze patterns evolved throughout each trial, with final fixations on decision targets occurring mainly in the last phase of action preparation. Focused visual strategies were more common in shooting and passing decisions, whereas broader search behavior’s characterized driving actions. These findings show that young players adapt their visual attention on a moment-to-moment basis in response to tactical demands, and support the relevance of in situ eye-tracking as a tool for understanding perception and decision-making in youth basketball.

title: Differences in the external and internal load according to the player’s position Diferencias en la carga externa e interna en función de la posición de juego Diferenças na carga externa e interna consoante a posição de jogo
abstract: Background/Objectives: the load analysis in football has consolidated as an essential factor for optimising performance and reducing the injury risk in players at different competitive levels. External and internal loads in football present significant changes according to the player position, and these differences must be considered in the training plan and periodization of the load during the season and in injury prevention. The study aimed to evaluate and compare external, internal, and neuromuscular load in senior football players in Portugal across different players’ positions. Methods: Wimu ProTM (Hudl, Nebraska, United States) and Garmin Heart Rate bands (Garmin International Inc., Kansas, USA) were used to quantify and evaluate the external and internal load of the players. A total of 121 athletes were assessed which were divided into 5 player positions. Results: significant differences were observed between players’ positions across several external and neuromuscular load variables (p >0.001). Considering the distance, midfields reported higher mean values (118.20±12.41) compared to the other positions. Considering the Player Load, significant differences were reported among the different positions (p <0.001; ε² = 0.285) and Total Impacts/min (p <0.001; ε² = 0.312). Regarding the internal load (heart rate), a significant difference was observed for the variable Avg. HR (bpm) (p = 0.024; ε² = 0.062) when comparing GK with all the other positions. In the same line, the GKs were those who reflected the lowest values according to the Avg. HR. Conclusions: the inclusion of kinematics, neuromuscular, and cardiac variables allows the coaching staff a higher comprehension of the sports performance and facilitates the decision-making of the performance manager.

title: Asociación de la maduración biológica sobre la composición corporal y rendimiento físico de adolescentes voleibolistas Association of biological maturation on body composition and physical performance of adolescent volleyball players Associação da maturação biológica com a composição corporal e o desempenho físico de jogadores de voleibol adolescentes
abstract: Introduction: In sports, adolescents of the same chronological age and with similar physical characteristics may differ in athletic performance and suitability for specific playing positions. Examining the relationships among peak height velocity (PHV), body composition, and physical performance may help identify patterns associated with athletic development and inform adjustments to training programs and nutritional strategies to enhance athletes' physical capabilities. Objective: To analyze the association between maturational age, body composition, and physical performance in adolescent volleyball players from Veracruz, Mexico. Methods: A total of 43 adolescent volleyball players from the Monsters League club in Veracruz, Mexico, participated in the study. Body composition and physical performance were assessed according to biological maturation status. Anthropometric measurements were obtained, and tests of speed, strength, and endurance were conducted. Discussion: Early maturers were characterized by higher VO₂max and lower body fat percentages, whereas late maturers showed higher speed and greater lower leg power, as indicated by better jumping performance. A greater number of moderate correlations (0.40 < r < 0.60) were observed among the variables assessed in early maturers, particularly between VO₂max and body mass index (BMI), compared with the other maturation groups. In contrast, strong and highly significant correlations were found among late maturers, particularly between VO₂max and jumping performance. Conclusions: The impact of maturation should be considered when evaluating physical performance and identifying athletic talent in youth sports.

title: Editorial: Winning by design: technology-integrated learning, performance, and recovery in team sports.
Rapid Acquisition of Complex Procedural Skills Using Simulation-Based Mastery Learning: A Multicenter Study in Gastroenterology Fellows.
abstract: Traditional apprenticeship-based procedural training is associated with variable learning outcomes and potential implications for patient safety. We assessed whether a simulation-based mastery learning (SBML) curriculum could enable novice gastroenterology fellows to achieve a predefined mastery benchmark in upper endoscopy. We conducted a multicenter, quasi-experimental study across six US gastroenterology fellowship programs. Participants were first-year fellows with no prior endoscopy experience assigned to SBML and second-year fellows who had completed 1 year of apprenticeship-based training. The SBML intervention consisted of a 5-day curriculum incorporating deliberate practice with expert coaching and required participants to meet or exceed a minimum passing standard (MPS) before completion. The primary outcome was performance on simulated upper endoscopy, assessed by blinded raters using a 6-point checklist (MPS = 4). Secondary outcomes included knowledge and self-efficacy. Twenty-six first-year fellows in the SBML group and 15 second-year fellows in the apprenticeship group participated. All 26 (100%) fellows in the SBML group achieved the MPS after 5 days of training, compared with five (33%) of 15 fellows in the apprenticeship group after 1 year (p < 0.001; odds ratio 22.8 [95% CI 3.8-136.0]). Mean checklist scores were higher (4.7 [SD 0.4] vs. 3.2 [0.7]; p < 0.001). Post-training knowledge and self-efficacy were comparable between groups. A structured 5-day SBML curriculum enabled novice gastroenterology fellows to achieve mastery-level performance in simulated upper endoscopy. Early competency-based training may accelerate skill acquisition and reduce variability versus apprenticeship.

title: Active Inference and Predictive Processing for Skill Learning: Implications for Skill Acquisition in Coaching Practice.
abstract: This paper explores the potential of the Active Inference Framework (AIF) and Predictive Processing (PP) to advance our understanding of skill and motor learning with a key focus on introducing these concepts to coaches and highlighting their practical implications. Conceptual frameworks such as Information Processing (IP) and Ecological Dynamics (ED) have contributed significantly to the field of skill acquisition. Despite recent efforts to reconcile these perspectives, however, their fundamentally different theoretical foundations concerning perception, cognition and learning processes pose substantial challenges for integration. Although ED has made valuable contributions through its focus on perception-action coupling and direct interaction with the environment, it involves adopting a radical ontological stance that emphasises rejecting traditional cognitive constructs that can complicate practical applications in coaching. Conversely, IP's reliance on concepts such as stored motor programs and the view of the brain as a computer-like processor can limit its ability to account for the dynamic, emergent nature of skill acquisition in real-world contexts. We suggest that AIF offers a parsimonious perspective, accommodating the dynamic, embodied and enactive nature of skill acquisition without the necessity of committing to either framework's specific assumptions. This perspective provides practitioners with a coherent and flexible framework for understanding and designing skill learning interventions, offering a practically useful account of skill acquisition for coaching practice.

title: From talent labels to stable expertise.
abstract: Early achievement and subjective labeling can be a weak guide to sustained expertise. Yet talent labels shape access to coaching, practice, and competition, so selection alters the conditions under which early judgements are later evaluated. This Perspective article proposes a conceptual framework in which labeling, selection, development, transition, and stabilisation are recursively linked processes. Its outcome, stable expertise, is repeated superior, domain-specific performance over a prespecified period that includes substantive changes in performance demands. The central claim is that the same outcome may reflect restricted opportunity, limited learning, difficulty adapting to new demands, or difficulty maintaining an established standard. Distinguishing these explanations requires separate observations of judgements, opportunity allocation, capacity change, adaptation, and performance over time. Five falsifiable propositions, each paired with a prospective design, specify when early indicators should lose predictive value, how selection shapes capacity through allocated opportunities, which junior advantages are unlikely to persist, and how adaptation, regulation, and support sustain or restore expert performance. The evidence is drawn mainly from sport; other domains require their own measures and tests. For talent systems, the framework implies treating labels as provisional predictions, reassessed against the opportunities they have created.

title: Using smart glasses technology to support the advanced skills competency of tissue viability nurses.
venue: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)
abstract: COVID-19 accelerated the use of technology in health care and forced health professionals to re-evaluate their approach to adopting new methods of healthcare delivery. In-person clinical supervision for new skill acquisition was often the only option before the COVID-19 pandemic. Today, with new technology available, supervising clinicians who are new to wound debridement has become easier via remote monitoring without sacrificing patient safety. This pilot project aimed to educate a cohort of four tissue viability nurses (TVNs) on wound debridement using smart glasses to overcome the lack of available in-person clinical supervision. Each TVN was remotely mentored by using Wi-Fi-enabled Vuzix M400 smart glasses to connect the TVNs and a supervising woundcare expert in real time. Remote supervision resulted in the TVNs becoming able to deliver timely wound debridement. By avoiding delays, they greatly reduced the risk of infection/sepsis in a highly vulnerable group of patients. This was achieved without sacrificing the quality of the supervision or patient safety; in fact, it facilitated the development of independent competency, improving patient safety in the long term. This method of clinical supervision is worthy of further exploration not restricted to wound debridement.

title: Mismatches Between Talent Identification and Development Models: Why Their Distinct Natures Must Be Nurtured.
venue: Perspectives on psychological science : a journal of the Association for Psychological Science
abstract: The identification and development of talent are top priorities across education, sports, business, and the arts. A major challenge lies in developing and applying appropriate models in both science and practice. Talent-identification models should center around predicting future excellence, whereas talent-development models should focus on how skills, resources, and their interactions change over time on the path to excellence. After providing an overview of the literature on talent-identification and talent-development models, I will argue that these models are often misapplied across domains: Talent-identification models are frequently used for talent development, and vice versa, which hampers progress in both scientific research and practical application. To address this issue, I propose a dual-path approach to nurture the distinct natures of talent-identification and talent-development models. For talent development, longitudinal processes involving relevant variables (e.g., psychosocial, cognitive, and physical) should be studied and evaluated at the individual level. For talent identification, predictive models incorporating relevant variables need to be tested, and their optimal and consistent application in real-world settings should be evaluated. This dual-path approach offers opportunities to advance psychological science and practice in identifying and developing talent across diverse domains of achievement.

title: When the Clock Is Wrong
abstract: Section: Preprints Categories: Sport Science, Elite Athletics, Measurement Keywords: soccer, athlete tracking, Sports events, data quality, performance monitoring, synchronisation Practitioners increasingly link coded match events to positional data to quantify the physical demands of individual actions, yet event timestamps are not perfectly aligned with tracking data. This study quantified how this misalignment affects event-level external load flags. Three elite German football matches (3,561 events, 61 players) with frame-level, hand-annotated event times served as ground truth. Four timestamp conditions were compared: the raw provider feed, a best-case constant clock correction and two synchronisation algorithms ( ETSY and ELASTIC ). Speed and acceleration flags were derived for the acting player in a ±2 s window and evaluated on 3,186 common events. Raw timestamps were misaligned by a median of 0.76 s, with 39.2% of events misaligned by more than 1 s. Using raw timestamps, 18.5% (95% CI 13.9–23.8%) of sprint-linked and 27.9% (24.4–31.4%) of sustained-acceleration-linked events were missed, and each additional second of error increased the odds of a missed flag 2.6- to 4.9-fold. A constant clock correction gave no significant improvement because errors were event-specific, whereas ELASTIC reduced misses to 1.0–2.1% (all p < 0.001). Event-level physical metrics should therefore be computed only after validated synchronisation.
